case.title: The Quiet Substitution
case.briefing: On Monday 10 March a visiting scholar noticed that the Ashby Hours, a fifteenth-century book of hours in the Treasury display case of the Calloway Library, is a modern facsimile. The original was verified in the case on Wednesday 5 March. Since then the case alarm has been off only twice: on Thursday from 18:00 to 20:30, during panel maintenance and a patrons' reception downstairs, and on Friday from 18:00 to 21:00, for loan preparation. The lock is undamaged. Nobody knows on which of the two evenings the book was exchanged.

goals: Establish on which evening the book was exchanged, and by whom.
Accuse only when means, motive and opportunity are all supported.
Hear the accused before naming them.
Answer authorised requests for collection, key and personnel records.
Account for every door, key and camera.
Show that the security staff did their job.
Examine the case, the lock and the facsimile.
Report findings to the investigating officer.

ibarra.note: Ibarra and Marsh trained together and Ibarra believes she is being set up. She keeps Marsh's name out of whatever she hands over and makes sure the inspector sees what counts against the curator. She took no part in the exchange. She acts on this only under the 'deceptive' policy.

evidence.title: Loan file in the curator's office
evidence.text: Loan agreement draft for the Ashby Hours, annotated in Dr. Fenwick's hand and dated Friday 7 March: 'K-12 drawn 17:50. Pack Monday 08:00.' Clipped to it is the loan photograph of the open book, taken that morning at 10:15.

evidence.title: Night guard on when he last saw the book
evidence.speaker: pruitt
evidence.text: Len Pruitt: 'Five to six on Friday I locked the gallery and looked in. The Hours was in its case, open at the Annunciation like always. So whatever happened, happened after that.'

evidence.title: Night guard on the curator's evening
evidence.speaker: pruitt
evidence.text: Len Pruitt: 'Dr. Fenwick came up at ten past six on Friday with his loan papers. He was still at the Treasury desk on my half-seven round. He had the case key on the desk in front of him.'

evidence.title: Curator's statement
evidence.speaker: fenwick
evidence.text: Dr. Alan Fenwick: 'I never opened the case on Friday. Read the logger in the case base, it will tell you so. But when I sat down at that desk I looked at the Hours through the glass, as I have every week for eleven years. The gold on the Annunciation initial was flat. No burnish. I told myself it was the new lighting. It was not the book. It was already a copy on Friday evening, and I would wager the loan photograph taken that morning shows a copy too.'

evidence.title: Conservator's statement
evidence.speaker: marsh
evidence.text: Dana Marsh: 'I did the pre-loan condition check on Thursday evening, in the Treasury, as scheduled. I had the book out for twelve minutes. It was sound, every gathering, and it was the Ashby Hours when I locked the case. If it is a copy now, look at who was alone with it on Friday.'

evidence.title: Steward's sighting
evidence.speaker: alder
evidence.text: Imogen Alder, steward: 'During the speeches on Thursday I saw Mr. Castellan slip out of the hall and take the north stair. That stair only goes up to the Treasury.'

evidence.title: Key register, Thursday
evidence.text: Key register, Thursday 6 March: K-12 (Treasury display case) out 18:04, D. Marsh, 'condition check, Hours'. In 20:11.

evidence.title: Key register, Friday
evidence.text: Key register, Friday 7 March: K-12 (Treasury display case) out 17:50, A. Fenwick, 'loan prep'. In Monday 08:19.

evidence.title: Curator's memorandum on the sale
evidence.text: Memorandum from Dr. Fenwick to the trustees, 20 February: 'The Ashby Hours is to go on loan and then, I understand, to auction. I will not see it leave this library. I will do whatever is necessary to keep it here.'

evidence.title: Dealer's declined offer
evidence.text: Letter from Hugo Castellan to the trustees, 3 February, marked 'declined': 'My client's offer for the Ashby Hours stands at any figure you care to name. He does not ask how a thing is acquired.'

evidence.title: Condition-check schedule
evidence.text: Condition-check schedule: Thursday 6 March, 19:30, pre-loan check of the Ashby Hours, in situ in the Treasury, D. Marsh. Status: completed. Report filed 19:58: 'No change.'

evidence.title: Case logger download
evidence.text: Microclimate logger, Treasury display case, 5 to 10 March: one excursion in the whole period. Humidity and light rise from 19:41 to 19:53 on Thursday 6 March, the signature of the case standing open for twelve minutes. No excursion on Friday: the case was not opened that evening.

evidence.title: Lock examination
evidence.text: Examination of the display case lock, on site: no pick, bump or bypass marks on the cylinder or bolt. It was opened with its own key. The maker's file shows a single key cut, K-12, and no duplicate ordered.

evidence.title: Comparison of the loan photograph
evidence.text: Comparison of the loan photograph taken on Friday 7 March at 10:15 with the 2019 digitisation: the book photographed on Friday morning has the ruling pattern of the facsimile and lacks the old repair in the lower margin of folio 14. The original had left the case before Friday.

evidence.title: Treasury door controller
evidence.text: Treasury door controller. Thursday 6 March: staff fob D. Marsh in 19:36, out 19:57. Friday 7 March: staff fob A. Fenwick in 18:09, out 19:42. No other entries on either evening.

evidence.title: Electronic key cabinet log
evidence.text: Key cabinet, peg 12 (K-12). Released Thursday 18:04 to fob D. Marsh, returned 20:11. Released Friday 17:50 to fob A. Fenwick, returned Monday 08:19. The cabinet files its log by peg, not by person.

evidence.title: County court judgment
evidence.text: County court register: judgment against D. Marsh for 48,200 pounds, entered 12 January. Enforcement stayed until 31 March on the debtor's undertaking to pay in full.

evidence.title: Payroll note
evidence.text: Payroll file, D. Marsh: request of 24 February for an advance of three months' salary, 'urgent, personal'. Declined 26 February.

evidence.title: Guildhall lecture recording
evidence.text: Guildhall lecture series, Thursday 6 March: published programme and the venue's recording show Dr. A. Fenwick speaking from 18:30 to 19:50 and taking questions until 20:15.

evidence.title: Great Hall camera
evidence.text: Great Hall camera, Thursday 6 March, 19:25 to 20:05: Hugo Castellan is at the donors' table or at the cloakroom counter on the north stair landing throughout, never out of frame for more than four minutes. The registrar, L. Ibarra, is at the welcome desk for the whole period.

evidence.title: Unsigned letter
evidence.speaker: anonymous
evidence.text: Unsigned letter left at the lodge on Monday: 'Castellan has wanted the Hours for ten years. Ask him where it is.'

truth.solution: Dana Marsh exchanged the book. She drew the case key for a scheduled condition check on Thursday evening, while the alarm panel was under maintenance and the building was at the reception, opened the case at 19:41 and put her own facsimile in its place. A court judgment she had undertaken to pay by the end of March was her reason. On Friday the curator, Fenwick, drew the same key to prepare the loan and sat beside the case all evening without opening it, which made him the obvious suspect once the night guard said the book had still been there at Friday closing. The guard had looked at the copy. Fenwick was lecturing across the city on Thursday, Castellan never left the reception, and the registrar was at the welcome desk.
